question.:question/problem:

from  $t=\frac{1}{2}$ to $t=\frac{9}{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,0,\,2t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+0+{(2t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8{t}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\,t\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}L&=\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\mathrm dt \\ &=\int_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1}(1/t+2t)\,\mathrm dt \\ &=(\ln t+t^2)\big|_{\frac{1}{2}}^{1} \\ &=\ln(1/\frac{1}{2})+1-\frac{1}{4} \\ &=\ln{\left(2 \right)} + \frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
